title: Window Function Comparison
description: Rectangular, Hann, Hamming, and Blackman windows shown in time and frequency, with main lobe width and side lobe level computed from a zero-padded transform.
creator: Real-Time DSP on a $5 Microcontroller
author: Dan McCreary
subject: Digital Signal Processing
Windowing
Spectral Analysis
chapter_title: Windowing, Spectral Leakage, and Peak Detection

educational.topic: Window functions and the resolution/leakage tradeoff
learningObjectives: Compare four windows in time and frequency domains
Distinguish the tradeoff each window makes
Choose a window for a stated measurement purpose

simulationModel.modelType: Zero-padded DFT of each window's coefficients
equations: Blackman: 0.42 - 0.5 cos(2 pi n/(N-1)) + 0.08 cos(4 pi n/(N-1))
assumptions: N = 64 window length, zero-padded to M = 1024 to resolve lobe structure
limitations: Covers four common windows; Kaiser and flat-top families trade differently and are not shown

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Identical dual-view layout across four options for direct comparison
keyQuestions: What do Hann and Hamming share, and where do they differ?
Which window would you choose to find a quiet tone beside a loud one?
commonMisconceptions: That a window improves the measurement for free
That lower side lobes are always the better choice
assessmentOpportunities: Select a window capable of a stated dynamic-range requirement
